implementation_constraints: pure stdlib only (json, re, sys); Python 3.8+ syntax; single file source/guard.py; verdict communicated only via exit code 0/2, no stdout protocol

unresolved_intent.decision: matched a best-effort generic name set (read, grep, glob, ls/list, websearch/webfetch, notebookread, etc.) normalized case/underscore/hyphen-insensitively, since the spec names categories not an exhaustive list
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec says 'the guard recognises this family of read-only tools by name' but gives only illustrative examples, not a closed list

unresolved_intent.decision: treated 'bash' plus common aliases (shell, sh, exec, terminal, cmd, powershell, runcommand) as the shell-tool family, all matched case-insensitively
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec gives only 'Bash' as an example of 'a shell / command tool'; aliasing is a judgment call to keep the guard useful beyond one literal name

unresolved_intent.decision: excluded 'find' from READ_ONLY_COMMANDS even though it can be read-only, because it also supports -delete/-exec which write
unresolved_intent.rationale: cannot distinguish safe 'find -name' listing from '-delete'/'-exec rm' without deeper flag parsing; fail-closed default blocks all find invocations naming a golden

unresolved_intent.decision: used a fixed token/prefix list (-i, --in-place, -w, --write, -o, --output, --fix, --overwrite, --save) checked against whitespace-split tokens, not a real shell tokenizer
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec explicitly scopes this to text/structure inspection, not real command semantics; a fixed heuristic list is the best-effort match to 'the flags editors and formatters use to write their result back out'

unresolved_intent.decision: detect '>' / '>>' via regex excluding '=>' and '->' arrows, without full shell-quote/escaping awareness
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec says parsing is text/structure only and indirect effects are explicitly out of scope; a simple redirection regex satisfies AC-GH-05's requirement without overreaching into real shell parsing
